and he gave all of them (or: gave it all) to the Tatars.
And they took [them] and went to Persia.
And after their departure,
there was a great famine and disease in Melitene and its territory,
and the land was filled with paupers, dying like beasts in the streets.
And many sold their sons and their daughters into slavery,
and no one would buy.
At this time 'Isa the physician of Edessa was renowned in Melitene,
who was the disciple of Hasnun the physician.
He moved from Melitene to Cilicia,
and entered the service of the king,
and he built in Sis a marvelous church in the name of the holy Mor Bar Sauma.
And in the year 1556
[1556] of the Greeks, the Tatars went to Baghdad,
and they were not able to capture it,
because a great multitude arose in fury against them
and turned them back frustrated.
And in this same year, Sultan Ghiyath al-Din was roused to jealousy,
and sent a multitude of troops to lay waste Cilicia,
because they had handed over his mother and his sister to the Tatars.
And the people of the territory of the Romans (Rûm) went and encamped against the city of Tarsus,
and waged a fierce battle against it.
And that Bailiff, the father of King Hethum, was present there with the Constable, his elder son;
and they too from within stood bravely against the besiegers from outside, through the many Franks whom they had with them.
And heavy rains and downpours came upon those outside,
and they began to be hard-pressed.
And they were unable to move anywhere in the region to bring provisions for themselves and their horses,
because of the bad mud that was there,
which almost swallowed horse and rider.
And while they were in this distress,
the news of the Sultan's death reached them,
and it was a relief to them;
and they abandoned [the siege] and departed from the region,
before this news was heard by the Armenians.
Now that Sultan Ghiyath al-Din died during the season of the Tishris (autumn),
at the beginning of the year 1557
[1557] of the Greeks.
And he had three young sons:
'Izz al-Din,
and Rukn al-Din,
and 'Ala al-Din.
And to 'Izz al-Din, who was the eldest among them, the grandees swore allegiance,
and they proclaimed him...
[and the Constable...]
the Amir Akhur of the king.
